name: Sahel insurgency
value: JNIM–IS Sahel rivalry; 64,000 fled to Niger
summary: JNIM and IS Sahel keep fighting each other; UNHCR says about 64,000 fled northern Nigeria to Niger in 2026
state: Africanews reported on 16 Oct that clashes between JNIM and Islamic State Sahel are intensifying in a turf war across the central Sahel, alongside both groups' attacks on state forces. UNHCR said on 10 Nov that violence in northern Nigeria has driven about 64,000 people into Niger this year (Reuters via Internazionale). Searches on 14 Nov found no fall or blockade of a capital or major city and no new mass-casualty spread to coastal states, so Watch holds.
for_you: Residents of rural Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger face attacks, blockades and displacement. FCDO advises against all travel to most of the region. Coastal states bordering the Sahel, including Benin and Togo, are exposed to spillover in their northern areas.
rubric_hit: Sustained insurgency at current levels (Watch); no capital blockade or coastal mass-casualty spread

sources.title: Africanews — Rival JNIM and Islamic State jihadists clash in intensifying Sahel turf war

why: Jihadist groups control growing territory across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, driving displacement and coastal-state spillover.
drivers: JNIM/IS-Sahel offensives, juntas, Russian forces, blockades, coastal-state attacks.
